title: Publisher SaaS Connector Onboarding: catalog copy + legal queries (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft to capture the marketplace catalog copy variants, technical/commerce acceptance checklist, and outstanding legal/compliance questions for Publisher SaaS connectors (3rd-party connectors listed in cloud marketplaces). The doc is aimed at GTM PMs, Partnerships, Marketplace Ops and Legal reviewers.

Audience / use cases:
- Marketplace listings (AWS/Azure/GCP) for SaaS connectors that integrate with Redwood Dedicated/Private
- Partner-facing onboarding: what we ask of publishers to get listed and billed correctly
- Internal readiness checklist for Marketplace Ops and Billing teams

Positioning statement (short):
- Variant A (concise): "Connect your app to Redwood Inference to serve low-latency LLM features across hosted and private deployments."
- Variant B (developer-focused): "Ship LLM-powered features faster. Our connector routes inference to hosted, dedicated, or private deployments with built-in observability and cost controls."
- Variant C (enterprise/secure): "Bring inference into your VPC — maintain data residency while getting production-grade throughput and SLAs."

2–3-line product description (for catalog):
- Short: "Redwood Inference connector enables [Publisher] customers to call Redwood-hosted and private inference backends from inside their product, with optimized latency, caching, and billing integration."
- Medium: "Install the Redwood connector to route user prompts to Redwood Inference with per-route policies, prefix caching for recurrent prompts, and integrated usage reporting. Supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC deployments for enterprise customers."

Top benefit bullets (for bullets area on marketplace page)
- Production-ready inference: low-latency streaming, KV cache, and autoscaling support
- Cost controls: batching and caching to reduce per-token cost with observable metrics
- Flexible deployments: hosted API, dedicated pools, or private VPC for regulated workloads
- Enterprise-grade: SLA-backed latency targets, audit logs, and KMS integrations

Call-to-action variants
- Install connector (1-click test deployment)
- Start free trial (limited credits for test prompts)
- Schedule demo with solutions engineering

Metadata we need to supply for listing (marketplace fields):
- Short product name (20 char max): "Redwood Connector" or "Redwood SaaS Bridge"
- Long description: use Medium product description above (editable)
- Category/tags: AI, ML inference, Developer tools, Integration
- Pricing model: Metered (tokens), SKU for monthly reserved capacity, trial credits SKU
- Listing images: 1 hero (PNG 1600x900), 3 screenshots (1280x720) showing console, latency dashboard, billing report
- Logos: SVG (square) and monochrome variant
- Support URL, Privacy URL, Terms URL

Technical acceptance checklist (Marketplace Ops + Eng)
- Connector technical docs uploaded (yes/no)
- Test harness: sample requests that cover short/long prompts, streaming, functions/tool-calls
- Sequence length test plan: 512/2048/4096 token matrix with latency percentiles
- Model variants: list of supported models and quantization profiles
- Billing integration: map partner usage to marketplace SKU or metered billing dimension
- Auth flow: OAuth2 client + scope requirements or API-key provisioning flow documented
- Network footprint: egress/IP ranges, VPC peering or PrivateLink guidance
- Security evidence: SOC2/ISO certs (file links) or equivalent statements
- Data handling: retention policy, log redaction, encryption at rest/in transit
- Failover modes: fallback model variants, regional fallback, and graceful degradation behavior

Commerce & billing specifics (operational notes)
- Proposed SKU mapping (example):
  - sku.redwood.inference.tokens = per-1k token unit (metered)
  - sku.redwood.dedicated.month = reserved capacity (monthly)
  - sku.redwood.connector.trial = one-time free credit
- Marketplace metering dimension must match our ingestion (tokens or request-units). Ops: ensure the marketplace metering export contains timestamp + partner-customer id + units.
- Minimum viable billing acceptance: sample CSV of 7 days usage for one test account and reconciliation script ready.

Legal & compliance open questions (to route to Legal/Privacy):
- Who is the data controller for prompt/response data once routed via connector? (publisher or Redwood)
- Is the connector considered a data processor? Does our DPA need specific language for connectors listed via partner marketplaces?
- Trial credit terms: do we require an additional partner invoice clause for trial conversions?
- Export controls / residency: what copy do we need to include for customers in EMEA/APAC?
- Logos and co-marketing: do we need a Partner Marketing Agreement signed before using Redwood marks in listing?

Required artifacts to attach for submission:
- Product one-pager (PDF)
- 2–3 screenshots with captions
- Architecture diagram (network, auth)
- Security certificate docs (SOC2, or table of controls)
- Sample billing CSV and SKU mapping doc
- Legal checklist signoff (GTM legal + Partner legal)

Internal timeline & owners (example sprint):
- Week 0: Draft copy variants + screenshots (owner: Maya)
- Week 1: Technical acceptance tests + sample usage export (owner: Eng Lead - Owen)
- Week 2: Legal review (owner: Priya)
- Week 3: Marketplace submission + vendor review cycle (owner: Partnerships - Ethan)

Acceptance sign-off matrix (single-line entries for portal):
- GTM copy: Maya - approved? __
- Eng readiness: Owen - latency & billing test results attached? __
- Legal: Priya - DPA language confirmed? __
- Marketplace Ops: Sofia - images & metadata uploaded? __

Open questions / TODOs (short running list):
- Decide canonical product shortName (Redwood Connector vs Redwood Bridge) - action: Maya
- Finalize SKU names and metering dimension - action: Owen + Billing
- Confirm whether trial must be a separate SKU in AWS marketplace (ask Marketplace Ops) - action: Sofia
- Legal clarity on data controller/processor roles for connectors - action: Priya

Sample copy snippets for listing (do not copy verbatim in final):
- "Ship AI faster: route prompts to Redwood's high-throughput inference runtime with predictable latency and observable cost per route."
- "Built for production: dedicated GPU pools, per-route rollouts, and automatic fallback policies keep features online."
- "Control cost and quality: batching, caching, and model recommendations tailored to your workload."

Notes about tone and constraints:
- Marketplace listings perform better when concise + benefit-led (3 bullets) + one clear CTA
- Use neutral legal-safe language around data; avoid committing to retention windows unless confirmed by Legal
- Keep performance claims conservative (e.g., "low-latency" rather than specific P50 unless verified by Eng test matrix)

Next steps before submission:
1) Pick final copy variant and shortName (Maya)
2) Upload screenshots and hero image to drive folder (Sofia)
3) Run 3-day billing export test and attach CSV (Owen)
4) Legal: provide approved DPA clause for connector listing (Priya)
5) Partnerships: open marketplace ticket and attach this doc + artifacts (Ethan)

Appendix: quick checklist for publisher onboarding form (to present to partners)
- Company name, legal entity, contact email
- Product shortName + one-line description (pre-filled from approved copy)
- Primary marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) and region targeting
- Required artifacts (attach architecture, screenshots, security docs)
- Billing mapping: do you use our SKU or your own resale flow? (select)
- Support SLA expectations and onboarding window

Comments/notes: please add inline comments in this doc in drive. This is intentionally a lightweight draft to get consensus before we generate final marketplace assets.
